label: Northwestern EDI · Team project
title: FamilySync
proposition: A family-care service concept that coordinates urgent handoffs without hiding consent or responsibility.
context: When a child needs help, care is only part of the work. Families also juggle calendars, permissions, pickup, medical context, and constant updates.
role: Service design · Research synthesis · Agentic interaction design

heroNotes.text: Urgent care is a coordination problem.
Keep caregivers connected and in control.

hero.alt: FamilySync concept showing Cynthia home with Leo while Robert and Stacy receive automatic updates
hero.caption: Automatic handoff updates keep absent caregivers connected without taking control from the person providing care.

sections.title: Care coordination is work
sections.intro: When a child gets sick at school, a parent is not solving one problem. Work, pickup, food, medical decisions, and family communication all arrive at once. We focused on the invisible coordination layer that becomes hardest when attention is already stretched.

storyNotes.text: A sick day creates several problems at once.

visuals.alt: Caregiver thoughts and coordination questions after a child becomes sick at school
visuals.caption: Work, pickup, food, medical decisions, and family updates collide in the same urgent moment.

sections.title: The family is the system
sections.intro: Care does not belong to one user. Parents, nearby relatives, schools, and clinicians hold different information and different authority. The concept had to make those roles visible without turning support into surveillance.

visuals.alt: Team Care research takeaways about care, control, trust, and privacy
visuals.caption: The research reframed proactive support around permission, privacy, and visible human control.

sections.title: Three principles shaped the idea
sections.intro: We organized the concept around three responsibilities: coordinate the work, communicate what is happening, and preserve the human connection behind the logistics.

visuals.alt: FamilySync pillars of coordination, communication, and connection
visuals.caption: Coordination, communication, and connection became the three responsibilities guiding the concept.

sections.title: Designing the handoff
sections.intro: The service is built around explicit handoffs. It checks availability, escalates through trusted caregivers, carries the right context forward, and shows the primary caregiver where they can step in.

storyNotes.text: Keep the caregiver able to step in.

visuals.alt: Large FamilySync schedule management and pickup escalation flow
visuals.caption: The pickup journey shows availability checks, escalation, confirmation, updates, and recap as one handoff.

sections.title: What I took forward
sections.intro: FamilySync changed how I think about agentic services. The useful part is not invisible automation; it is making intent, permission, uncertainty, and escalation understandable at the moment someone needs to trust or interrupt the system.

storyNotes.text: Keep the system easy to interrupt.

closingContext: Student team project created at Northwestern EDI with JPMorgan Chase as project partner; not a shipped product.
